defect: fetch_txt now calls get(url, polite=False), which skips _common.polite_sleep. That is the only per-request pause enforced for data.rada.gov.ua: politeness.py:67-70 marks the Rada policy row reference-only and says 'today Rada politeness is _common.polite_sleep + budget.py bytes'. The Rada TXT collector therefore sends requests back to back with no minimum interval, and the byte budget named as the replacement caps daily volume, not request rate.
consequence: An A-03 run with editions to fetch hits Rada as fast as the server answers. Whenever a response takes under 1 s the run goes over Rada's <=60 req/min and skips the mandatory 5-7 s pause. That invites 429s (persistent ones fail the editions and the run exits 1) or Rada's temporary anti-DDoS IP block (403, 'back off in HOURS' per reachability.py:10-12), which would also stop the other data.rada.gov.ua collectors on that IP. The over-limit run itself reports ok and exits 0, so the operator is not told.
proof: I rebuilt the pre-change module in memory: the same file with line 78 reverted to 'r = get(url)'. I ran main() of both versions with --acts 2747-15 over 300 editions of 60 KB each. The DB, the budget, file writes and httpx.get were mocked, and a virtual clock replaced time.monotonic and time.sleep, with the server answering after a fixed latency. BEFORE, at 0.1/0.3/1.0 s latency: at most 10 requests in any 60 s, minimum gap 6.00 s. AFTER: 300/201/60 requests in any 60 s, minimum gap 0.10/0.30/1.00 s (the latency alone), 0 s of pause in total. In every run the budget used 18.0 of 180 MB and never deferred, and the run returned exit=0 with 'COLLECT-SUMMARY ok=300 failed=0'. The limits are written in the tree: _common.py:3-5 ('<= 60 req/min with a 5-7s pause', MANDATORY) and politeness.py:67 (Rada <=60/min). The get() docstring at _common.py:60-61 reserves polite=False for 'a burst of Range reads against one already-open resource', while fetch_txt fetches a different edition URL each time. Every other Rada caller keeps the default pause: fetch_cards.py:96, fetch_attachments.py:72, ksu/snapshot.py:106. No test in tests/ references fetch_texts or fetch_txt (Grep), so the suite cannot catch this.
